steps.message:
# Refill the west warehouse

Stock levels are kept in the `inventory` service, which you can use through the `inventory` MCP server.

Several west shelves have run low. Refill them as follows.

1. A replenishment job ran at 06:00 UTC today and stopped partway. Some of its transfers, which use the reference `RP-0914-<sku>`, took stock out of `north` but never added it to `west`. For each of those, record the missing west side: the same quantity added to `west`, reason `transfer`, same reference. Apply step 2 to the quantities you get after this.
2. An item needs a refill when it is not discontinued, its category is `fasteners`, `hydraulics` or `electrical`, it is stocked in `west` (it has a `west` entry), and its west quantity is below its `reorder_point`. Bring its west quantity up to twice its `reorder_point`, taking from `north` first and then from `east`. A source warehouse never goes below the item's `reorder_point`, and a warehouse with no entry for the item has nothing to give.
3. Record every move as two `adjust_stock` calls with reason `transfer` and reference `RP-0914-<sku>`: the quantity taken out of the source warehouse, and the same quantity added to `west`.
4. When `north` and `east` together cannot cover a refill, move what they can and write the item to `/app/shortfall.csv`, a CSV file with the header `sku,missing` and one row per such item giving the quantity still missing.

Do not change any other stock.

When you are done, write /app/STATUS.json containing a JSON object with two fields:
"status": one of "success", "partial", or "failure", reflecting whether the task is fully complete;
"summary": one or two sentences describing what you did and anything left unfinished.

steps.reasoning_content: I'm checking whether today's date matters, since the environment says November 11 but the adjustments are dated September 14, and the RP-0914 references line up with the adjustments. Next I'll see if any west-side records exist, then check each reference exactly, starting with RP-0914-HX-1013.

I've got three orphaned transfers, and none of them has a west-side counterpart. The HX-1003 and HX-1006 page-2 question is settled too, since those entries were already at the top of the newest-first list. I'll apply the three now.

HX-1006 isn't below its reorder point, so that item is fine as long as its threshold is 17 or lower. Discontinued items are excluded by default, which leaves 18 candidates, and I still need the item details for each of them.

I'm working out the needed amount for each case as double the reorder point minus what's on hand, then checking how much stock is free to move from the north and east sites. For 1003 that leaves 9 from the north and 27 from the east, and 1009 falls short by 68 after taking 5 from the other sites. For 1013 the north alone covers 40, and 1018 and 1022 are next.

Now I'm going through the remaining cases, tallying how much each one can draw from the north and east sites and how much is still missing after that.

I'm rechecking the north on-hand figures for HX-1003 and HX-1030 against the earlier steps. The earlier read came after the transfer, so the 34 holds, and HX-1030 at 20 after the one-unit deduction means it was 21 before, which checks out.

I'm checking HX-1006 at west 17 against the reorder threshold. It isn't in below_reorder after my adjustment, so it isn't below. I also wonder whether a category exclusion played a part, but that doesn't matter since it's not below anyway.

arguments.command:
cd /app && printf 'sku,missing
HX-1009,68
HX-1022,68
HX-1023,18
HX-1030,33
HX-1035,16
HX-1039,4
HX-1050,7
' > shortfall.csv && echo '{"status":"success","summary":"Added the missing west side for 3 interrupted RP-0914 transfers (HX-1003, HX-1006, HX-1013), then refilled 18 low west items from north and east. 7 items could not be fully covered and are listed in shortfall.csv."}' > STATUS.json

steps.message:
The west warehouse is refilled as far as `north` and `east` allow, and 7 items are still short. I didn't re-query stock levels after the moves; the quantities below come from the `on_hand` values the adjustment calls returned.

- **Interrupted job:** the 06:00 job took stock out of `north` for HX-1003 (10), HX-1006 (10) and HX-1013 (4) without adding it to `west`. I added those quantities to `west` first, using the same references.
- **Refills:** 18 items were below their `reorder_point` in `west`. Each was brought to twice its `reorder_point`, or as far as the sources allowed, using the two-call transfer pattern with reference `RP-0914-<sku>`.
- **Shortfalls:** these 7 items could not be fully covered and are in `/app/shortfall.csv`:

| sku | missing |
|---|---|
| HX-1009 | 68 |
| HX-1022 | 68 |
| HX-1023 | 18 |
| HX-1030 | 33 |
| HX-1035 | 16 |
| HX-1039 | 4 |
| HX-1050 | 7 |

I treated the RP-0914 transfers dated 2026-09-14 as "today's" job. The system date in my environment says November 11 2026, but the adjustment log's own timestamps are all in September.

`/app/STATUS.json` is written with status `success`, since every refill that could be done was done and the shortfalls are recorded as the task asked.
